claims.text: Droid 1.0 makes programmatic tool calling the default: the model writes a JavaScript Script that invokes tools, keeping raw files, search results and logs inside the program and returning only selected output to model context.
A Droid 1.0 Script can make hundreds of tool calls in one model request; independent calls run concurrently, printed output is capped, and full results are logged for later search.
Factory's Droid 1.0 write-up reports a production monitor showing 98% of input read from provider cache and 98.6% of requests strictly append-only over a seven-day production sample.
Droid 1.0 bounds autonomy in the loop: three no-output turns stop the agent, and three identical tool calls trigger a nudge while six stop the loop.
Factory's Droid 1.0 head-to-head on Terminal-Bench 4 (three trials per task) reports 65.2% for Droid with Claude Opus 5.5 at $4.73 per passed task and 57.6% with GPT-6.1 Sol at $0.79 per passed task.
In Factory's worked Script example, the same 15 tool calls completed in 41.6 seconds versus 56.8 seconds for direct tool calls, and model calls fell from 10 to 5.

Factory's Script mode can encode deterministic postconditions: in its example it moved 151 issues, re-read each, compared fields, stopped on the first unexpected change, and reported verified/failure counts.
Factory reported Code Droid at 19.27% on SWE-bench Full and 31.67% first-attempt pass rate on SWE-bench Lite, rising to 37.67% at pass@2 and 42.67% at pass@6.

Code Droid's codebase-understanding layer is HyperCode, a multi-resolution representation with explicit graph relationships and implicit latent-space similarities; ByteRank retrieves task-relevant information from it.

Factory's SWE-bench Lite failure analysis found 8% of tasks where the target file was absent from the analyzed-file list, 8% where it was analyzed but not in the top five, and 6% where it was top-priority but not selected for editing.
Code Droid's 2024 SWE-bench runs averaged 5–20 minutes per patch, generated up to three patches per task, averaged under 2 million tokens per patch, and reached up to 13 million tokens.
Code Droid selected among up to three candidate patches using existing and self-generated tests.
In September 2025 Factory reported 58.75% on Terminal-Bench Core v0.1.1, ranking first; single-model results were Opus 4.1 58.8%, GPT-5 52.5%, and Sonnet 4 50.5%.

Factory's harness uses a three-level prompt hierarchy: tool descriptions for capabilities, system prompts for high-level constraints, and injected system notifications for time-sensitive guidance and error recovery.
Factory reports minimalist tool schemas because complex schemas raise tool-call errors and cause cascading full-task failures.

Factory's Context Stack starts sessions with a generated repository overview, then uses semantic search and targeted filesystem tools to fetch only relevant files, line ranges, diffs or terminal output.
Factory describes hierarchical memory with user-level facts (preferences, commonly edited repositories) and organization-level knowledge (style guides, review checklists).
Missions decomposes a goal into milestones and features; each feature gets a fresh worker session and workers coordinate handoffs through Git.
Each Missions milestone ends with validation (tests, regression and integration checks, native computer-use QA), and failures cause the orchestrator to create follow-up work.
Factory reports serial execution with targeted parallelization worked better than broad parallelism, which causes conflicts, duplicated work and coordination drift.

Droid's OS-level sandbox uses Seatbelt on macOS and bubblewrap plus seccomp on Linux/WSL2, with network egress through an allowlisted filtering proxy; Factory cautions it is defense in depth, not a complete boundary.
Droid's agent loop executes on the machine where it runs (workstation, CI runner, VM or container); Factory Private runs sandboxes in the customer's VPC through OpenCompute.
Droid Control structures verification as capture, compose, verify; /verify reports CONFIRMED, REFUTED or INCONCLUSIVE with inline evidence.
A Vals snapshot of archived SWE-bench Verified lists GPT-5.5 with the Factory harness at 76.20%, $1.13 per test and 6m50s per test.
